kept.title: Prototype Pollution via recursive object assignment
kept.description: The `assign` function (src/scimPatch.ts:437) does not sanitize input keys, allowing an attacker to set arbitrary properties on object prototypes (e.g., `__proto__`, `constructor`) when processing patch values.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a SCIM Patch request with an 'add' operation
Set the path to '__proto__'
Set the value to an object containing malicious keys
Observe that the application's global object prototype is now modified
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) or Denial of Service by modifying the behavior of built-in objects.

kept.title: Sensitive Information Leakage in CI logs
kept.description: The CI pipeline uses `npm install -g` with sudo and runs tests while outputting to logs. CI environments are often exposed to third parties, and dependencies installed this way may inherit environment variables or secrets.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger a build on a PR from a fork
Observe CI logs for exposed secrets or credentials
Access build logs to steal environment information
kept.impact: Exposure of development tokens, secrets, or internal infrastructure details.

kept.title: Unsafe Dependency Management via Automerge
kept.description: The `.kodiak.toml` configuration enables automatic merging for pull requests by 'dependabot' for minor/patch updates, creating a high risk of malicious code injection if a dependency account is compromised.
steps_to_exploit: Compromise a package used by the application
Submit a benign-looking 'patch' upgrade via Dependabot
Wait for Kodiak to automatically merge the malicious code into production
kept.impact: Supply chain compromise via automated malicious code deployment.

kept.title: Use of 'any' type creates safety gaps
kept.description: ESLint is explicitly configured to allow 'any' types in TypeScript. This hides type-related security bugs and makes the codebase susceptible to runtime crashes and injection attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Pass unexpected object types to the `scimPatch` function
The code proceeds without validation, leading to undefined behaviors
Exploit those behaviors to crash or alter the resource object
kept.impact: Reduced reliability and hidden security vulnerabilities throughout the business logic.

kept.title: Insecure Git checkout in CI workflow
kept.description: The CI workflow uses `actions/checkout@v2`, which is outdated and may be vulnerable to known security issues in handling submodules or symlinks.
steps_to_exploit: Create a repository with malicious git submodules
Trigger the CI pipeline
The outdated checkout action may execute malicious scripts during the process

kept.title: Implicit trust of 'any' type in SCIM operations
kept.description: The patch operations rely on casting object properties to `any`, bypassing TypeScript's static analysis to check if keys exist or are mutable.
steps_to_exploit: Send a patch with an path referencing internal application state properties
The logic blindly navigates to these internal nodes
Modify critical internal application state
kept.impact: Manipulation of internal application objects, potentially leading to unauthorized privilege escalation.

kept.title: Unrestricted deep cloning via JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())
kept.description: The use of JSON-based deep cloning is unsafe; it can result in loss of data (e.g., Date objects, RegEx) and can be used to perform Denial of Service attacks on memory.
steps_to_exploit: Send a very large or deeply nested SCIM resource object
The application attempts to clone it using JSON serialization
Observe memory exhaustion and performance degradation
kept.impact: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Excessive permissions for Github Token
kept.description: The PR auto-assign workflow uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` with default write permissions, which could be abused if a developer's workflow or CI script is compromised.
steps_to_exploit: Modify an existing workflow file to print the token
Exfiltrate the token to an external server
Use the token to modify repository settings or create malicious pull requests

kept.title: Incomplete validation of patch operations
kept.description: The code allows operations with lowercase or mixed-case 'op' values but doesn't strictly enforce input bounds, leading to potential discrepancies between the RFC and the implementation.
steps_to_exploit: Send an unknown operation type (e.g., 'update')
The system might interpret the operation incorrectly or crash due to unexpected behavior in the switch-case block

kept.title: Potential bypass of array filtering constraints
kept.description: The regex used to detect array searches is simple and might be bypassed, leading to incorrect path resolution.
steps_to_exploit: Use a path containing unusual characters that bypass the IS_ARRAY_SEARCH check
Force the system to treat a non-array path as an array

kept.title: Use of outdated ESLint version
kept.description: The dependency list uses an extremely old or incorrectly versioned `eslint` (10.4.0 is not currently a public/stable release; likely a misconfiguration or dev-only issue).
steps_to_exploit: Install dependencies with npm
The system uses unverified or potentially malicious packages if versioning is hijacked

kept.title: Lack of rate limiting
kept.description: The library acts as a processor for user-provided patch operations. Without external rate limiting, it is susceptible to resource-heavy processing of large patch arrays.
steps_to_exploit: Send multiple, massive JSON documents in a single request
Exhaust server CPU resources during deep-copy and nested loop operations

kept.title: Unsafe usage of 'delete' operator
kept.description: The `delete` operator is used on object properties, which is generally discouraged in JavaScript engines because it can cause de-optimization and is potentially unsafe depending on the object type.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a patch that triggers the deletion of system-critical properties (e.g., meta or schemas)
The application continues executing with corrupted state

kept.title: Implicitly trusting external input in filters
kept.description: The `filterWithQuery` function directly parses and executes string-based queries without strict sanitization.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a malicious filter string intended to access hidden object attributes
The parser executes this against the resource

kept.title: Non-standard license usage
kept.description: The project uses 'Unlicense', which can pose legal risks for enterprise adoption and lacks clear protection for maintainers.
steps_to_exploit: Deploy code in a corporate environment
Observe legal compliance issues regarding code origin and liability
